_comment: Plan 002 §7 P9/P3 — language-neutral credential.get vectors: what an app is allowed to put on the socket. `expected_keys` is the EXACT key set of the frame (the `id` is a per-request UUID, so it is compared for presence, not value): a CSR-less request omits the `csr` key entirely rather than sending an empty string, which is what makes an mtls server's refusal legible. `max_csr_bytes` caps what we are willing to send. `forbidden_substrings` is the key-containment assertion (§7 P3): the app relays a PKCS#10 CSR — public material — and the private half never leaves the Rust core, so none of these markers may appear in ANY app→agent frame. The list covers PEM armour AND the base64 DER prefixes a raw PKCS#8/SEC1 key encodes to, because the realistic accident is not a PEM block pasted into the frame — it is a private key handed to the CSR parameter, which would look like ordinary base64. Markers are matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY, so a fixture carrying a real CSR must be checked against this list when it is added.
_forbidden_note: The base64 markers are the DER prefixes real keys encode to, verified against openssl output: MIGHAgEAMBMGByqGSM49… / MBMGByqGSM49AgEGCCqGSM49AwEHBG… (PKCS#8 EC P-256, the curve the core generates — the second is the length-independent inner form), MHcCAQEE… (SEC1 EC), BgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAASC (PKCS#8 RSA, the length-independent inner form).

vectors.name: without_csr
vectors._note: a token-only client; an mtls server answers with its own explicit upgrade error.
